title: Elastic Serverless project API key as the encoded value of an Authorization ApiKey header
summary: A synthetic encoded Serverless project API key after the ApiKey scheme of an Authorization header, in a raw request, a curl option and a JSON header map.
rationale: Elastic documents that after a Serverless project API key is created, the encoded key is copied and sent as an Authorization: ApiKey header value to the Elasticsearch HTTP API (claim encoded-carrier). Elastic calls the Serverless personal key the equivalent of the stack personal key and one response type defines the encoded member for both (claims stack-page-calls-serverless-keys-equivalent, serverless-create-response-type-is-shared), so the envelope is shared with the Elasticsearch user API key and with the Cloud API key; the contract records an issuance-context role, not a distinct shape, and reuse of the envelope proves nothing about a shape. The case states the span for this family only and does not edit the existing Authorization ApiKey Case. No width, alphabet or padding is claimed; each fixture value is the base64 of a fixed synthetic id and key. The extent is the value after the scheme only. Contract claims cited: serverless-project-api-key/encoded-carrier, serverless-project-api-key/stack-page-calls-serverless-keys-equivalent.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#243). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value after the ApiKey scheme of an Authorization header is treated as a credential for a Serverless project key. Elastic documents the carrier (carrier existence only); the value admission, the extent and the shared-envelope attribution are the project's decisions.

sources.supports: Once created, you can copy the encoded API key and use it to send requests to the Elasticsearch HTTP API: -H "Authorization: ApiKey ${API_KEY}"
To create equivalent keys for Serverless projects, refer to serverless-project-api-keys.md.
sources.locator: tip after the list of key types

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
